paper_section_text:
\paragraph{Native pilot of the released math library.}
A separate phobos-vt point uses the release's Lean~4.34.1 toolchain,
Mathlib revision \texttt{d13f23b7} and eight matching dependency pins.
Seven modules covering four preselected targets are compiled serially with
one Lean thread, a 200,000-heartbeat option, an 8,192\,MiB native memory
option, \texttt{autoImplicit=false} and olean-only output.
Source text is unchanged in these seven modules.
Prerequisites and OS caches are already warm; their preparation is outside
the per-compiler clocks.

Each module runs first without profiling/stats and then with native
\texttt{--profile} only. All 14 compiler processes exit zero without a
sorry warning. This does not establish transitive axiom closure or full
candidate-service acceptance. Baseline and profiled process-wall sums are
44.003 and 44.499 seconds; CPU sums are 44.044 and 44.530 seconds.
The observed wall difference is 0.496 seconds, or 1.13\%, in one fixed-order,
shared-node pair, without randomized repetitions or a population bound.
The complete two-mode capture is 89.078 seconds.
Compiler-process high-water RSS reaches 7.46\,GiB, while the one-second
sampled aggregate peak is 7.43\,GiB; sampling can miss shorter peaks.
Neither the native memory option nor those samples are a hard RSS quota.

This is four of the 53 selected targets, not complete representative native
coverage or a full-library timing. Cumulative profiler phases overlap and
are not a wall partition. Version, option, cohort, budget and compilation
boundary differ from the \texttt{trace.profiler} diagnostic in
Table~\ref{tab:profiler-diagnostic-limits}; this observed difference cannot
rescale that truncated-work point or establish engine acceleration.

A separate expanded point follows the next three targets in the original
53-target frame, with 128 new closure-module states at 50,000 heartbeats,
no profiling/stats and one Lean thread. It actually invokes 82 compiler
processes: 81 exit zero without a sorry warning and one reaches a
\texttt{whnf} heartbeat limit in the \texttt{ProjectionCoordinates}
dependency. The remaining 46 dependent modules are explicitly uninvoked,
with no assigned timing or native verdict. Two target endpoints compile;
the third is not invoked after that dependency boundary. This does not
establish an invalid theorem or failure of an unbounded upstream build.

Compiler-process wall sums are 218.436 seconds, with 187.020 user-CPU and
31.291 system-CPU seconds. The complete capture is 225.245 seconds.
Its one-second sampled combined W-tree peak is 11.87\,GiB, including the
retained earlier EPFL process, and is not a hard quota or whole-node peak.
These module clocks use a separate resource point from the initial seven
200,000-heartbeat profiled modules; they do not complete all 53 targets,
calibrate full-library costs or establish transitive axiom closure.

A subsequent incremental point retains the 81 successful dependency
objects and attempts the other 47 modules at 100,000 heartbeats. All 47
compile without a sorry warning, including the previously interrupted
dependency. The 128-module closure and all three target endpoints are then
available across the two budget points. The fresh 47-call process-wall sum
is 102.649 seconds, inside a separate 110.118-second capture. This does not
retroactively turn the 50,000-heartbeat failure or uninvoked states into
passes, supply a fresh single-budget build time, or prove general budget/
runtime monotonicity. Including the earlier pilot, 135 distinct compiled
objects are available; their full imported axiom status remains unestablished
by compiler exits alone.

A native metadata reader subsequently inspects all 135 serialized objects.
It finds 1,799 theorem declarations, including 743 auxiliary-name theorems.
Lean's native expression equality gives 601 auxiliary-type keys, or 604
groups when ordered universe parameters and private-name status are added;
45 groups span modules. These are typed producer observations, not complete
state or replay keys. In the five files containing this pilot's 45
\texttt{decide +kernel} source occurrences, the reader identifies 45
\texttt{of\_decide\_eq\_true}-headed auxiliary proofs with distinct native
type keys. This pilot therefore demonstrates no merging of those 45 calls
by exact type equality. It excludes the large repeated-goal
PlanarPacking/Ramsey clusters, failed calls and uninvoked producers.
It supplies neither whole-corpus native counts nor failure-cache
coverage. Transitive axiom closure, hidden-state dependencies and replay
qualification remain unmeasured; reading objects is not checking them again.

A wider unprofiled point selects nine more targets from the original frame
and one unweighted public repeated-text probe. Among 171 new closure modules,
109 native invocations yield 108 compiler successes and one self-wall
interruption; 62 dependent modules are not invoked. Seven of the nine
original target endpoints compile. The module-wall sum is 724.589 seconds
inside a 732.836-second capture, with a 12.20\,GiB sampled combined tree
that includes the retained old EPFL process.

The interrupted 1.82\,MB \texttt{PlanarPacking.Grid} source consumes
151.397 user-plus-system CPU seconds before its 120.094-second self-alarm.
Requested \texttt{-j1}/\texttt{LEAN\_NUM\_THREADS=1} is therefore not a
measurement of one OS thread. CPU-active compilation differs from the
sleeping EPFL case, but these clocks do not attribute the Grid cost to
a tactic, kernel phase or hardware bottleneck. The blocked public probe's
16 repeated source annotations occur under 16 namespaces; neither their
text equality nor namespace differences establish resolved native type
identity. The accumulated points leave 243 distinct compiled objects,
including 14 endpoints of the 53-target frame. This is availability across
resource points, not a fresh homogeneous build clock, completed frame,
transitive axiom audit or population estimate.
